messages:
Maya (marketing): Hey team — prepping the launch blog + webinar. We need a concise, reproducible bench dataset and validation checks to back our claims about gen latency and cost. Can runtime help with a focused rerun and a small smoke checklist?
Priya (eng-runtime): Yep — can do. Can you list the exact configurations and the deliverables you need? p50/p95/p99, token counts, and raw logs ok?
Maya (marketing): Exactly. Ask: 1) p50/p95/p99 latency per model/variant, 2) tokens generated (avg & distribution), 3) cost-per-1k-tokens estimate using current pricing, 4) raw request/response logs (anonymized), 5) artifact: short reproducible script + curl payloads for press. Also want quantized vs fp16 comparisons and cold vs warm KV cache.
Ethan (runtime): Understood. Proposed minimal matrix: models [redwood-rl-13b, redwood-rl-70b], variants [fp16, int8-q4], sequence lengths [64, 256, 1024], batch sizes [1, 8, 32]. Workload: 1k samples per cell for stable stats. Is that overkill for marketing?
Maya (marketing): 1k sounds fine but if cost/time is an issue, 200 samples per cell is OK for the PR table — we still need a longer run (1k) for the appendix. Prioritize the 256-length row for the main slide.
Priya (eng-runtime): Ok we'll do 200 samples for the headline run and queue a 1k background sweep for the appendix. Need seeds and sampling params.
Maya (marketing): Use deterministic sampling: temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, seed=42. Also include a small set of burst traffic tests: 100 concurrent short requests (len=64) and a sustained throughput run (10 QPS for 10 minutes) to show tail behavior.
Liam (data-ops): For the raw logs, we'll scrub prompt content and user identifiers, keep model/variant/runtime-metrics, trace ids. We'll produce a CSV with per-request: timestamp, model, variant, seq_len, batch_size, latency_ms, tokens_out, cpu_gpu_util.
Ethan (runtime): Plan: run smoke checklist first: (a) single-sample sanity for each model/variant, (b) KV cache warmup test (10 prefix requests then measure), (c) quantized fallback correctness check (sample outputs compare BLEU-like quick diff). If smoke passes, start headline matrix.
Maya (marketing): Timeline: need headline numbers and a reproducible script by EOD Friday for copy review. Appendix runs by next Tue. Can you hit that?
Priya (eng-runtime): EOD Friday for headline 200-sample matrix is tight but doable if we limit concurrency. We'll target it. If anything slips, we'll ping here.
bench-bot: run queued: job_id=rb-2026-09-29-001 matrix=[models:2 variants:2 lengths:3 batches:3 samples:200]. ETA ~5h for smoke + headline.
Ethan (runtime): I'll paste a sample curl for the reproducible snippet below. Use this in the blog's reproducibility appendix.
Ethan (runtime): ```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rl-13b", "variant":"int8-q4", "input":"Summarize: ...", "max_tokens":256, "temperature":0.2, "top_p":0.9, "seed":42}'
```
Maya (marketing): Perfect — include a short blurb on methodology that explains sample sizes, seed, and anonymization. Also call out that p99 from burst runs is with cold-starts included. :thumbsup:
Priya (eng-runtime): Will do. I'll drop the headline table and the reproducible script here when ready.
Maya (marketing): Thanks all — tagging @Priya @Ethan for visibility.
